title: Marcos rejects call to reassess economic team amid 'malaise'
summary: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Friday stood by his current economic team even as he was urged by a senator to take a closer look at his Cabinet amid a so-called “economic malaise.”

blocks.text: President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. on Friday stood by his current economic team even as he was urged by a senator to take a closer look at his Cabinet amid a so-called “economic malaise.”

In a Kapihan with the media in Shenzhen, China, the President said he disagrees with the call of Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson, who earlier raised concerns about the dipping Philippine stocks, the weakening peso, and rising inflation, among other issues.
“No, I don’t…I disagree with him. I’m sorry, but I disagree with him,” Marcos said.
“All the difficulties we’re going under can be clearly directly traced to the war in Iran,” he added.
Marcos likewise addressed speculations about recent changes in his Cabinet, saying that he is only trying to “put the best people to the best use” amid developments worldwide.
“Everything was done for a particular reason. There’s no general reason that I’m not happy with the Cabinet or anything like that. No, not at all. Quite the contrary,” he said.
“Issues come up that didn’t exist before in certain departments. So we’re trying to put the people who are best able to address those issues into the proper department,” he added.
The President said that the reshuffle also had something to do with his administration’s plans.
“[We’re] trying to get the best people into whatever position we need to best be able to push our priorities for the future,” he said.
Marcos also stood firm that shifting one Cabinet member to another position does not produce instability in the government.

“The job of a Cabinet secretary does not remain exactly the same from day one until day whatever it is six years later. Nagbabago talaga ‘yan (it really changes). And then we make our own plans as we go along,” he said.

“And then we have to worry about shocks like the war in Iran, so we have to adjust also to that. And then now with AI coming up, we have to adjust also to that. And then the different developments in geopolitics, we also have to adjust to that,” he added. —LDF, GMA News
